title: Advertising and Salesmanship
summary: Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods and services by an identified sponsor (American Marketing Association). Its features: paid communication, non-personal (through mass media), promotes goods or services and has an identified sponsor. Publicity is a non-paid form of communication, such as news in the mass media about a product or organisation; it can be favourable or unfavourable and the firm has no control over its content. Advertising versus publicity: paid versus not paid; identified sponsor versus none; full control over message versus no control; favourable impression intended versus may be favourable or unfavourable; target is prospective buyers versus the general public.

Objectives of advertising: introduction of a new product; increase in sales; maintaining existing buyers; creating and enhancing the goodwill of the firm; dealer support; creating and enhancing brand image; helping personal selling. Advantages: to manufacturers (introduce products, retain and attract customers, goodwill, makes salesmen's job easier, fights competition); to consumers (useful information, right use, comparison, information for remote areas); to society (competition improves products through R&D, educates, generates employment, revenue to media makes newspapers and programmes affordable). Limitations: multiplies wants; adds to cost and price; creates monopoly; may affect the value system; motivates wrong or dangerous deeds (liquor, cigarettes); may not increase overall demand (shifts demand between brands); one-way communication.

Newspapers suit mass-consumed goods and services (banking, insurance) but not products with few buyers (industrial products, designer jewellery). Television reaches all segments including illiterate consumers with visuals and sound, suits mass-use goods and new products but is costly. Radio reaches rural and semi-urban people (e.g. Krishi Sandesh) and FM radio reaches urban commuters. Magazines and journals reach specific segments (sports goods in sports magazines, medicines in medical journals). Films suit mass-consumption goods (cosmetics, toiletries) but are costly with limited reach. Outdoor advertising (hoardings, walls, neon signs, vehicular displays) catches people travelling; it is cheaper than print or television but has limited reach. Internet advertising allows direct interaction and low-cost reach to young, tech-savvy consumers.

Salesmanship (personal selling) is assisting and persuading prospective customers to buy a product in a face-to-face situation. Steps in the selling process: prospecting (identifying prospective buyers); pre-approach (gathering information about the customer); approach (gaining attention); presentation and demonstration; answering queries and objections; action or closing the sale; follow-up or after-sales service. Importance: to consumers (guide and friend, explains use, gives confidence, after-sales information), to business (increases sales, identifies new customers, feedback for product improvement, explains technical products) and to society (facilitates production, distribution and consumption, market information, matches demand with supply, informs about new products, growth of business).

Qualities of a good salesperson: good personality; mental qualities (alertness, imagination, foresight, empathy); good behaviour (patience, humility, cooperation); knowledge of the product, company and competitors; ability to communicate and persuade; persistence.

Sales promotion means short-term, temporary incentives to induce trial or purchase, other than advertising, salesmanship and publicity (e.g. 'buy one get one free'). Objectives: to attract new customers, increase short-term sales, introduce a new product, clear excess stock and counter competition. Tools: rebate, discounts, refunds, product combinations, quantity gift (extra quantity), instant draw and gift scheme, lucky draw, usable benefits (free offers), full finance at zero interest, sampling (free samples, e.g. a sachet of shampoo attached to a magazine) and contests.

vsa: State any two limitations of advertising.
It multiplies wants and adds to the cost and price of products.
Any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods or services by an identified sponsor.
Differentiate between advertising and publicity on any two bases.
Advertising is paid and has an identified sponsor; publicity is unpaid and has no identified sponsor.
Assisting and persuading prospective customers to buy a product through face-to-face communication.
Name any two objectives of advertising.
Introduction of a new product and increase in sales (also goodwill, dealer support).
What are the benefits of advertising to society (any two)?
It generates employment and makes media available at affordable prices.
Why is knowledge of the product important for a salesperson?
It lets the salesperson answer queries, explain features and use, and persuade the customer with confidence.
sa: State any three qualities of a good salesperson.
Good personality, thorough product knowledge and the ability to communicate and persuade (also persistence and good behaviour).
State any three objectives of sales promotion.
To attract new customers, to increase sales in the short run and to introduce a new product.
Explain any three advertising media and state their suitability.
Newspapers suit mass-use products and services; television suits mass-use goods and new products and reaches the illiterate; magazines suit a selective target segment.
Differentiate between advertising and sales promotion.
Advertising is a non-personal, paid, long-term communication through media; sales promotion is a short-term incentive for immediate purchase.
Explain any three tools of sales promotion.
Discounts, free samples and contests (also rebate, refunds, lucky draws).
Explain the benefits of salesmanship to consumers.
The salesperson guides and informs the customer, explains how to use the product and gives after-sales information.
Explain any three advantages of advertising to manufacturers.
It introduces new products, increases sales by attracting customers and builds goodwill.
la: Explain the steps in the selling process.
Prospecting, pre-approach, approach, presentation and demonstration, answering objections, closing the sale and follow-up service.
New product introduction, increase in sales, retaining buyers, goodwill, dealer support, brand image and helping personal selling.
It multiplies wants, adds to cost, creates monopoly, affects values, promotes dangerous deeds, may not raise total demand and is one-way communication.
Explain the qualities of a good salesperson.
Personality, mental qualities, good behaviour, knowledge, ability to communicate and persuade and persistence.
Explain the importance of salesmanship to consumers, business and society.
Consumers get guidance and information; business gets more sales and feedback; society gets smooth production, distribution and consumption.
Explain the media of advertising with their suitability.
Newspapers, television, radio, magazines, films, outdoor media and the internet with their reach, cost and suitable products.
